question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

events.title: Xi Jinping out before 2027?

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's firm grip on the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced through extensive anti-corruption purges targeting military and civilian elites including recent Politburo removals, underpins the 95.5% trader consensus against his removal before 2027. With no designated successor and the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027 expected to endorse a fourth term, institutional norms and elite networks aligned with his leadership show no credible challenge. Ongoing discipline-focused plenums and the absence of visible factional fractures further support expectations of continuity. A sudden health event, unprecedented congress postponement, or coordinated elite realignment could still shift outcomes, though credible reporting finds no evidence of such developments materializing.

eventMetadata.context_description: The wide-open 2028 Democratic field features no declared candidates and a pronounced gap between national polling, where Kamala Harris often leads, and prediction markets favoring Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Jon Ossoff, and Gavin Newsom. Traders appear to discount Harris after her 2024 loss while assigning premium value to younger profiles with rising visibility: Ocasio-Cortez’s strong performance in early-state surveys such as New Hampshire, her recent comments leaving a White House bid open alongside possible Senate ambitions, and renewed DSA ties; Ossoff’s sharp anti-administration messaging and Senate reelection fundraising momentum despite his repeated denials of interest; and Newsom’s consistent national profile through state actions and travel. The DNC’s finalization of a South Carolina-first primary calendar and the focus on November midterms further sustain uncertainty, keeping top probabilities clustered as the party weighs progressive versus moderate directions ahead of any formal announcements.

The DNC’s finalization of a South Carolina-first primary calendar and the focus on November midterms further sustain uncertainty, keeping top probabilities clustered as the party weighs progressive versus moderate directions ahead of any formal announcements.
